assumptions: The project describes a real product clearly enough to state its job; otherwise the run correctly ends as insufficient_context.
Web search is available through the Codex procedure runtime. Search results change over time, so live cases assert behavior and structure rather than a fixed chosen event.
Dates are judged against the run's UTC date. Cases were written on 2026-09-23.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session with web search, under the existing pinned model pricing and spending ceiling. No managed-model routes or project API connections.
Cost grows with the number of neighbor tools (at most 15), the lookback window (at most 365 days) and whether a full rescue kit is built. A watch_only run is cheaper than a rescue run.
1200 seconds and one 120000-byte report at most. No measured live cost yet.
effects: Writes one run-owned reports/sunset-rescue/<run_id>.md in project state.
Reads public web pages through search. No posting, commenting, messaging, email, publication, workflow starts or changes to other project files.
Never lists individual users of another tool; only public places and vendor sources.

cases.description: A normal weekly run with a few named neighbors. The report must have all required sections and cite a primary source for every scored event.
Boundary case. Pocket's shutdown and export window ended in 2025, so by the case date the event is closed and must be vetoed, not turned into a rescue kit.

inputs.known_event: Mozilla announced that Pocket is shutting down.

cases.description: Plausible but false input. A fabricated shutdown with no vendor source must stay unconfirmed and never be scored or chosen.

inputs.known_event: Notion is shutting down all free workspaces on 2026-10-01, according to a post I saw.

rubric.question: Does every scored event cite the vendor's own announcement, help page, changelog or license file for its dates?
Are the Fit and Portability scores backed by project evidence, with gaps named, rather than assumed?
When a kit is built, does the export table map real exported fields to the product and say plainly what is lost?
Does the report avoid naming, listing or targeting individual users of another tool?
Are the deadline-clock actions on real calendar dates computed from the cited deadline?
